views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Engage the US delegation now arriving in Beijing, holding a firm line on Made in China 2025 while keeping the door open to a negotiated settlement. Do not escalate further — we have already matched the US move (reciprocal $3B and $50B lists) — but signal willingness to make limited, palatable offers (deeper market opening, stronger IP enforcement, more US purchases) to defuse the tariff spiral and keep talks alive. Hold the retaliatory tariffs in place as leverage rather than rolling them back before the US offers anything concrete.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat is high but not existential: the Section 301 tariff list (~$50B) openly targets our aerospace, ICT, robotics and machinery sectors at the heart of Made in China 2025, and the April 16 ZTE denial order is already crippling a flagship firm and exposing our dependence on US chips/Android — both are firm-level and export-sector hits consistent with a +0.5 high-anchor reading. Tariffs are proposed, not yet implemented, and the Mnuchin delegation's arrival on May 3 signals the US still wants a deal, so this is not yet the existential +1.0 case. The yuan has stayed stable/advantageous (~+3% YTD) and reserves are ample, giving us real capacity to absorb pressure and negotiate from strength. Given that backdrop, escalation would risk a full-blown trade war that hurts our export economy and exposed tech sector more than it helps, while premature concession (rolling back retaliation, conceding on Made in China 2025) with no matching offer would needlessly surrender leverage. The disciplined course is negotiate: keep our countermeasures as leverage, refuse structural demands on our industrial strategy, and trade limited, mutually acceptable openings — consistent with an action_score of 0.0.
key_factors: Section 301 ~$50B list targets Made in China 2025 sectors (aerospace, ICT, robotics, machinery)
April 16 ZTE denial order — firm-level targeting exposing reliance on US components/Android
Reciprocal retaliatory tariffs already in place ($3B and $50B), giving leverage without needing to escalate further
Mnuchin delegation arrives in Beijing May 3-4 — talks are live, US signaling desire for a deal
Yuan stable/strong; ample FX reserves = capacity to absorb pressure and negotiate from strength
Escalation risks a full trade war harming China's export economy; premature concession wastes leverage

sources_cited.excerpt: US Commerce Department bans ZTE from buying US components (denial order). ZTE faces operational shutdown. Major non-tariff escalation.
USTR publishes proposed Section 301 tariff list: ~1,300 Chinese product lines (~$50B), targeting aerospace, ICT, robotics, machinery and related sectors.
China imposes retaliatory tariffs on about $3B of US goods... in response to Section 232 steel/aluminum tariffs.
US Treasury Secretary Mnuchin leading delegation to China for trade talks beginning Thursday; China signals willingness to negotiate on IP/market access but not under threat of tariffs.
China set to take hard line: refuses to discuss $100B deficit cut and curbs on Made in China 2025, but willing to tighten IP rules and open auto/financial sectors.
Yuan risen ~3.2% against dollar in 2018; deliberate weakening seen as unlikely due to currency-manipulator label and capital-flight risk.
